partners.mechanism_chain: PNLIP (HGNC:9005) —DISRUPTS→ Pancreatic Triacylglycerol Hydrolysis (REACT:R-PPC-162036); Pancreatic Triacylglycerol Hydrolysis (REACT:R-PPC-162036) —DECREASES→ Free Fatty Acids (CHEBI:37735); Free Fatty Acids (CHEBI:37735) —LEADS_TO→ Fat malabsorption (HP:0001387); CEL (HGNC:2203) —DISRUPTS→ Glucose Homeostasis (GO:0001988); Glucose Homeostasis (GO:0001988) —LEADS_TO→ Diabetes Mellitus (HP:0000829). Loss-of-function mutations in PNLIP lead to pancreatic triacylglycerol lipase deficiency, impairing fat digestion and absorption, manifesting as fat malabsorption. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in CEL disrupt glucose homeostasis, leading to diabetes mellitus. While the direct enzymatic functions are distinct (fat digestion vs. a role in maintaining pancreatic beta-cell function or insulin secretion), both genetic disruptions impact distinct yet interconnected physiological modules within the pancreatic and metabolic systems, leading to distinct but potentially overlapping phenotypic consequences.

#### 1. maturity-onset diabetes of the young type 4  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.410)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9925561)

**Proposed mechanism:** CEL (HGNC:2175) —DISRUPTS→ insulin secretion pathway (REACT:R-HSA-190826); PDX1 (HGNC:9540) —DISRUPTS→ insulin secretion pathway (REACT:R-HSA-190826); insulin secretion pathway (REACT:R-HSA-190826) —LEADS_TO→ Impaired insulin secretion (HP:0011877); Impaired insulin secretion (HP:0011877) —LEADS_TO→ Diabetes mellitus (HP:0005978). Loss-of-function mutations in CEL (causing MODY8) and PDX1 (causing MODY4) both converge on disrupting the insulin secretion pathway in pancreatic beta-cells, ultimately leading to impaired insulin secretion and diabetes mellitus.

**How to falsify it:** If mutations in PDX1 do not impair the insulin secretion pathway or if mutations in CEL do not impact the same pathway, this hypothesis would be falsified. Additionally, if a specific variant in PDX1 is found at a high frequency (>1%) in the general population (e.g., gnomAD), it would cast doubt on its specific role in MODY4. _(variant: rs11551362)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of PDX1 and downstream pathways in MODY4 and MODY8 could lead to targeted therapeutic strategies for both forms of diabetes, potentially involving pathway modulation or gene therapy approaches focused on preserving beta-cell function.

While the direct enzymatic functions are distinct (fat digestion vs. a role in maintaining pancreatic beta-cell function or insulin secretion), both genetic disruptions impact distinct yet interconnected physiological modules within the pancreatic and metabolic systems, leading to distinct but potentially overlapping phenotypic consequences.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of mutations in PNLIP in individuals diagnosed with MODY8, or absence of mutations in CEL in individuals diagnosed with pancreatic triacylglycerol lipase deficiency. _(variant: High frequency (>1%) of pathogenic variants in PNLIP or CEL in general population databases like gnomAD.)_
